after: ## What are the HL regional options? (90 hours, HL only)
alt: HL students study one of four regional options and three of its eighteen sections. Paper 3 sets two questions on each section, 36 in all; about six fall on the three sections studied, and students answer three. Paper 3 is worth 35% at HL.
caption: Only about six questions will be on your sections, so revise all three fully.

after: ## What is the internal assessment? (20 hours, SL and HL)
alt: A bar of 25 marks split into three sections: identification and evaluation of sources, 6 marks; investigation, 15 marks; reflection, 4 marks. The investigation is up to 2,200 words on a topic of the student’s choice, marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, and worth 25% at SL and 20% at HL.
caption: The investigation section carries 15 of the 25 marks.

after: ## How should you use this syllabus?
alt: The prescribed subject (one of five, 40 hours) is assessed in Paper 1, worth 30% at SL and 20% at HL; two world history topics (90 hours) in Paper 2, 45% and 25%; the HL regional option (90 hours) in Paper 3, 35% at HL; and the historical investigation (20 hours) as internal assessment, 25% and 20%.
caption: At HL, Paper 3 carries more weight than any other single component.

after: ## What changes for first exams in 2028?
alt: Side-by-side rows compare the course examined until 2027 with the course first assessed in May 2028: the prescribed subject becomes a 50-hour focused study, the world history topics become an 80-hour thematic study, the 90-hour HL regional option becomes a 90-hour regional study, the 20-hour investigation loses its separate reflection, and six key concepts become four paired concepts.
caption: The 2028 course reshapes every component; it does not affect exams in 2027 or earlier.
